planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 5.0-6.5), humus-rich soil in partial shade; Plantation Pink is a fast, vigorous grower well suited to hedge and screen training from a young age.

directions: Plantation Pink is a fast-growing, large sasanqua camellia bred by E.G. Waterhouse in Australia in 1948, producing abundant, softly fragrant, pale-to-medium pink flowers with a loosely layered petal arrangement and bright golden stamens from October into winter. Its vigorous, upright, arching habit reaches 8-12 feet tall in the Gulf South, making it one of the larger sasanqua selections, well suited to hedging, screening, and background plantings rather than tight foundation spaces. Grow in acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil with a layer of mulch over the root zone, and protect from harsh afternoon sun and drying wind, which can scorch the glossy dark-green foliage. Established plants tolerate short dry spells better than most camellias, but consistent moisture during bud set in late summer improves fall bloom quality.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 5.0-6.5), humus-rich soil in partial shade to full sun; Pink-A-Boo is a patented sport of 'Yuletide' with a similar dense, upright-arching habit.

directions: Pink-A-Boo, sold under the trade name Pink-A-Boo and registered under the cultivar name 'Mondel', is a fragrant sport of the popular red-flowered 'Yuletide' that arose with the same dense, upright, gracefully arching branch structure but hot-pink, single-to-semi-double flowers accented by prominent bright-yellow stamens. Bloom runs from fall into early winter on a vigorous shrub reaching about 8-10 feet tall and wide at maturity, making it a strong choice for screening or as a large specimen where a saturated pink counterpoint to the more common white and red sasanquas is wanted. Grow in acidic, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade to filtered sun, since sasanquas tolerate more light than japonica camellias but still benefit from afternoon protection in the Gulf South. Feed with an acid-forming camellia fertilizer in early spring and again after bloom, and prune only immediately after flowering to avoid cutting off next season's buds.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 5.0-6.5), humus-rich soil in partial shade to full sun; Rainbow can be trained as a large shrub or limbed up into a small multi-stem tree form.

directions: Rainbow, introduced by Nuccio's Nurseries in California in 1956, is a vigorous, large sasanqua camellia bearing fragrant single flowers to about 3 inches across, with white petals edged in soft pink and a conspicuous cluster of golden-yellow stamens at the center - a distinctive bicolor look among mostly solid-colored sasanquas. Blooming from fall into early winter, it grows into an upright large shrub or small tree, eventually reaching 8-15 feet, and can be limbed up as a specimen or kept denser with light pruning for screening. Plant in acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade to filtered sun, with protection from harsh afternoon exposure, and mulch to keep roots cool and evenly moist. Because Rainbow flowers heavily on the current season's wood, prune only immediately after bloom to preserve next year's flower display.
